correctness.rationale: For any instruction sequence the signs at odd indices alternate on successive odd sites, bounding run length by three. An ordered pair of complete runs of lengths a,b corresponds uniquely to an exterior-flanked word of length a+b+2<=8. In every such window exactly one index is divisible by eight; the other seven letters are determined by the first three instructions and the start residue modulo sixteen. The exceptional sign is asymptotically equidistributed conditional on that residue by summing the odd-quotient classes at all 2-adic valuations, independently of instruction tails. The complete 32-template enumeration for every instruction triple yields the integer matrix ((0,3,1),(3,2,3),(1,3,0)). Its sum 16 establishes pair density 1/2 per sign position, and division gives run-pair frequencies matrix/16. Exact mutual-information arithmetic is checked. The standalone verifier executes the symbolic enumeration and independently checks the recursion; long-prefix tests are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The mathematical claim is the explicit limiting pair-frequency matrix, independent of every folding instruction, with a precise two-run mutual-information value. Published paperfolding abelian-complexity and canonical-factor results address different observables; the closest full paper (Shallit, arXiv:2412.17930) gives run-length automata, allowed run lengths, possible squares, and subword complexity but does not compute or assert this invariant pair-frequency law. value.rationale: The result supplies a complete two-point statistical law for the run coding of every paperfolding instruction sequence, including nonautomatic ones. The instruction-independent weights are not determined just by knowledge that {1,2,3} are the possible run lengths or by factor-support restrictions. The rational joint matrix gives an exact nonzero adjacent-run mutual information and establishes a natural probabilistic invariant of an uncountable deterministic family. This is a motivated structural classification, not an arbitrary short prefix or small numeric improvement.
